name: Underworld Breach
oracle_text:
Each nonland card in your graveyard has escape. The escape cost is equal to the card's mana cost plus exile three other cards from your graveyard. (You may cast cards from your graveyard for their escape cost.)
At the beginning of the end step, sacrifice this enchantment.
blocked_sentences: Each nonland card in your graveyard has escape. The escape cost is equal to the card's mana cost plus exile three other cards from your graveyard.

needs.what: an additional-cost rider on the `cast_from_graveyard` static -- a Cost charged on top of the granted spell's own mana cost, drawn from `cost_keys`, so this card's static can carry `exile_from_graveyard: {"count": 3, "exclude_self": true}`. It must be priced and paid by `legality.graveyard_cast_permission` / `Game._cast` at the moment the granted spell is cast (the way `chosen_additional` charges a card's own `additional_cost`), and `exclude_self` has to mean the card being escaped, not the permanent granting the permission -- otherwise a three-card graveyard pays for the escape with the escaping card itself.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cast_from_graveyard` is the only static that lets a card out of a graveyard and it grants the cast at the card's printed cost with no price attached. Its whole rider vocabulary is `enters_tapped`, `arrived_this_turn_from` and `affects_spells`; the one cost field on any permission static is `pay_life_instead`, which belongs to `cast_from_library_top`, swaps mana for life rather than adding to it, and cannot express an exile. The card-level `graveyard_cost` / `flashback` slot *is* escape and does carry `exile_from_graveyard` with `exclude_self` -- but it is a field on the escaping card itself, set at load time, and Underworld Breach hands escape to cards it has never seen. There is no op or static that writes a cost onto another card, and `grant_keyword` knows only the 34 ability keywords, none of which is escape.

needs.what: an unbounded `cast_from_graveyard` permission -- `static_max_per_turn` made optional (or given an explicit unlimited spelling) for permissions whose price is itself the rate limit, with `legality.graveyard_cast_permission` skipping the `GRAVEYARD_CAST_SLOT` ledger check instead of defaulting `cap` to 1. Underworld Breach prints no cap at all; the three exiled cards per cast are the whole brake.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The loader hard-refuses `cast_from_graveyard` without `static_max_per_turn` (`if not model.static_max_per_turn`), on the stated grounds that a permission with no rate limit is an unbounded engine rather than a printed line -- which is true of Edgar, Master Machinist's "once during each of your turns" and exactly false of this card. Every accepted value is a finite integer, so any number I could write would be a cap this card does not print: the card is a storm/loop enabler and an invented ceiling is the approximation, not a rounding of one.
